title: Left Hop Converter
description: Pin the unit you have and the unit you want, hop the measure left one place at a time, and watch the number divided by 10 at each hop, then clip the unit onto the decimal.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Change a measure from a smaller unit to a bigger one by counting the places from the unit you have to the unit you want and dividing the number by 10 for each, write a mixed measure as one decimal, split a measure into two units, and name the unit of every decimal.
writeup.look: One row of the unit chart with digit tiles in its columns, two pins for the unit you have and the unit you want, and a point that hops left.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Left Hop Converter' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of hops the point has made. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. One row of the chart runs across the middle of the area at y 380: seven columns, each 140 wide, from x 90 to x 1070, headed kilo to milli with the base unit in the middle and the unit names violet, labelled Unit. The given measure stands in deep blue digit tiles, labelled Given, one to a column, with the point in the gap after its unit. The deep blue have pin stands over the unit you have at y 300, and the green want pin is dragged along the same line to the unit you want. The Hop button stands at x 900, y 230. Each hop moves the point one gap to the left and draws a vermilion arrow under the row along y 470, labelled Move, divide the number by 10. A grey zero, labelled Place holder, drops into any column between the point and the digits that would otherwise stand empty. The Cut handle is a short upright bar that slides along the gaps of the row. The unit tags wait in a tray at x 120, y 560, and the answer is read in green, labelled Answer, at x 120, y 660, only once a tag is clipped to it. The unit in use is amber. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a point key and a delete key. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the nine tools of this chapter share them. The measure the question gives, in the unit it is given in, is deep blue, labelled Given or Measure. The measure the working reaches, and a reading on a scale, is green, labelled Answer, Reading or Same measure. The places moved across the unit chart, and the worth of one small mark on a scale, are vermilion, labelled Move or One mark. A unit fact, the unit names on the chart and the other temperature scale are violet, labelled Unit fact, Unit or Other scale. The part taken away, and a part left over after sharing, are rose, labelled Taken away or Left over. The unit, column, mark or step being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open inside a number, labelled Place holder, and for nothing else. Rulers, tapes, jugs, scales, thermometer tubes, chart lines, arrows, operation signs and step labels are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of the content colours, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The last measure stays on the row with its hops drawn beneath, its point after the unit wanted and its unit tag clipped on.

phases.win: the point stops after the metres digit, and the two hops glow vermilion beneath
phases.does: drags the want pin to m, counts the places between the pins, and hops the point once for each
phases.goal: count the places from the unit you have to the unit you want; each place to the left divides the number by 10
phases.says: Pin the unit you want. How many places away is it?
phases.check: Away from the screen: from millimetres to centimetres, which way do you go, and how many places?
phases.feels: the point sliding left and the number shrinking while the length stays the same
phases.hands: Draw the chart's seven columns on paper and write a length in centimetres, one digit to a column. Put a coin on centimetres and another on metres, count the steps between them, and move a paper point one column left for each.
phases.tries: First rung: pin the unit you want and count the places without hopping. Second rung: hop once and read the measure. Third rung: the same task between two neighbouring units, one place apart, before the question's own measure returns.

wrong.why: a change of unit feels like it should make the number grow
wrong.move: hops the point to the right instead of the left
wrong.screen: the point stays where the child put it and the measure is read back in that form with its unit, far more than the card shows; the pins light amber, and the places between them are counted again one hop at a time in vermilion

wrong.why: counting on fingers touches every column, not every step
wrong.move: counts the columns the pins stand on as well as the steps between them, and hops once too often
wrong.screen: the extra hop reads the measure back in the unit one place further left, and the steps between the two pins are drawn one vermilion arrow each, in steps

phases.screen: a length in centimetres set in the row, the have pin on cm and the want pin loose
phases.soWhat: count the places from the unit you have to the unit you want; each place to the left divides the number by 10

phases.win: a grey zero drops into the empty place, and the decimal in kilograms turns green
phases.does: sets the point after the kilograms digit and fills the empty place
phases.goal: a mixed measure is one decimal in the larger unit, with zeros holding empty places after the point
phases.says: Where does the point go? Is any place empty?
phases.check: Away from the screen: in a weight of some kilograms and a few grams, which places after the point are empty?
phases.feels: a grey zero dropping into a gap and the whole decimal turning green
phases.hands: Write a weight in kilograms and grams on the paper chart, the kilograms under kg and the grams in their own columns. Set a paper point after the kilograms and fill any empty column with a zero.
phases.tries: First rung: set the point after the kilograms digit only. Second rung: put each grams digit in its own column. Third rung: the same task with no empty column, before the question's own weight returns.

wrong.why: the two numbers look as if they can simply sit either side of the point
wrong.move: writes the grams straight after the point with no zero in the empty place
wrong.screen: each digit is read back from the column it now sits in, showing far more grams than the question gave, and the empty column is lit amber with a grey zero waiting beside it

wrong.why: the grams are the last thing written, so the point feels like it goes at the end
wrong.move: sets the point after the last grams digit
wrong.screen: the point stays and the measure is read back in grams, while the kilograms pin and its column are lit amber

phases.screen: a weight in kilograms and grams, its two parts in their own columns, one place empty between them
phases.soWhat: a mixed measure is one decimal in the larger unit, with zeros holding empty places after the point
phases.concept: A mixed measure as one decimal

phases.win: the measure falls into two cards, metres and centimetres, both green
phases.does: drags the Cut handle to the metres column and reads the two parts
phases.goal: a measure in one unit can be split at a unit's column into a larger unit and a smaller one
phases.says: Cut it where the metres end. What is left in centimetres?
phases.check: Away from the screen: how would you say the length of your bed in metres and centimetres?
phases.feels: one long measure splitting cleanly into a metres card and a centimetres card
phases.hands: Write a length in centimetres on the paper chart. Lay a pencil upright in the gap after the metres column, and read the digits to its left as metres and those to its right as centimetres.
phases.tries: First rung: point to the metres column. Second rung: cut there and read the metres part. Third rung: the same task on a shorter length, before the question's own length returns.

wrong.why: the handle feels like it should sit near the end of the number
wrong.move: drags the Cut handle one gap too far to the right
wrong.screen: the two cards are read back in the units the cut gives them, and the gap after the metres column is lit amber

wrong.why: the metres feel like the answer the question wants
wrong.move: types only the metres part as the answer
wrong.screen: the metres card turns green, and the centimetres card beside it is lit amber and waits to be read

phases.screen: a length in centimetres with the Cut handle resting beside the metres column

phases.win: the tag clicks onto the decimal and the whole measure turns green
phases.does: clips the unit tag the decimal is in, and sees the same digits read in another unit beside it

phases.screen: a capacity in litres and millilitres, its decimal built, and a tray of unit tags
phases.soWhat: every decimal is written with its unit, because the same digits in another unit are another measure

writeup.delight: On the third phase, when the Cut handle drops into the right gap, the row splits in two and the metres half and the centimetres half slide apart into two green cards, each with its own unit tag already clipped on.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet hopped. On the first phase a length in centimetres sits in the row, one digit to a column, with the have pin on centimetres and the want pin lying loose above. On the second a weight's two parts sit in their own columns with one place empty between them. On the third a length in centimetres sits in the row with the Cut handle resting beside the metres column. On the fourth a capacity's decimal is built with a tray of unit tags beside it. One thing moves, once: the want pin, the point, the Cut handle or the tag tray gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any measure set on any row, pinned and hopped left to any bigger unit, cut into two units, and tagged. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on counting places, mixed measures as one decimal, splitting into two units, and naming the unit of a decimal.
voiceLines: A measure on the chart, and a pin on its unit.
Pin the unit you want. How many places away is it?
Where does the point go? Is any place empty?
Cut it where the metres end. What is left in centimetres?
Which unit is this decimal in? Clip it on.
A new measure. Pin the unit you want.
Free play. Set any measure and hop it anywhere to the left.
Look at the two pins. How many places apart are they?
You hopped left to a bigger unit, and named it.

observations.why: a bigger unit needs fewer of itself to make the same length.
observations.soWhat: moving to a bigger unit divides the number, never the thing measured.
observations.observe: Each hop to the left made the number smaller, but the length on the card stayed the same.

observations.why: each unit is 10 times the unit to its right, so each place is one divide by 10.
observations.soWhat: count the places from the unit you have to the unit you want before hopping.
observations.observe: The number of hops was the number of places between the two pins.

observations.why: each place after the point is one unit of the chart, and an empty one must be held open.
observations.soWhat: the zero keeps every digit in its own unit's column.
observations.observe: A grey zero dropped in wherever a place after the point had no digit.

observations.why: the unit decides what each digit is worth.
observations.soWhat: a decimal is only a measure once its unit is written with it.
observations.observe: The same digits read with another tag named a very different measure.

phases.screen: a length in centimetres set in the row, the have pin on cm and the want pin loose
phases.win: the point stops after the metres digit, and the two hops glow vermilion beneath
phases.traceback: The pins light amber, the point goes back to the unit you have and hops left one place at a time to the want pin, ending on the measure in green.
ladder: How many places to the left of cm does m stand?
Pin L, then count the hops from mL.
Where does cm stand on the chart, compared with mm?
Each hop to the left divides the number by 10.
Count only the steps between the two pins, not the columns they stand on.

phases.screen: a weight in kilograms and grams, its two parts in their own columns, one place empty between them
phases.win: a grey zero drops into the empty place, and the decimal in kilograms turns green
phases.traceback: The pins light amber, the point hops from the smaller unit to the bigger one, a grey zero drops into each empty place, and the decimal turns green.
ladder: Is every column between the point and the 6 filled?
Where does km stand on the chart, compared with m?
Look for a column with no digit before you read.
Every digit stays in its own column while the point hops.
A zero must hold each empty place between the point and the digits.

phases.screen: a length in centimetres with the Cut handle resting beside the metres column
phases.win: the measure falls into two cards, metres and centimetres, both green
phases.traceback: The Cut handle slides to the gap after the bigger unit's column, the row splits in two, and both parts turn green with their unit tags.
ladder: Cut where the metres end, then read both parts.
Cut after m and read the decimetres on their own.
Cut after kg; the grams are the digits on its right.
Read each part in the unit of its last column.
The cut goes right after the column of the bigger unit.

phases.screen: a capacity in litres and millilitres, its decimal built, and a tray of unit tags
phases.win: the tag clicks onto the decimal and the whole measure turns green
phases.traceback: The point hops to the unit asked for, the empty places get their zeros and the unit tag clips on in green; for the two weights each tag is clipped in turn and the digits move three places.
ladder: Check the empty place and the unit tag, then type the number again.
Check the columns after kg and the unit tag, then type the number again.
Clip each tag and see where the digits go.
The unit tells you which column the point sits after.
Read from the point to the last digit, zeros included.
From cm to m is two places, so hop the point twice to the left.
Two hops divide by 100: read the digits with the point after the m column.
Count the gaps between the two pins, not the columns.
A bigger unit always stands to the left, so the point hops left.
mm and cm stand next to each other: one hop to the left.
One hop divides by 10; read the measure in cm.
Hop until the point sits after kg; that is three hops.
Read every digit after the point in order, the grey zero too.
km stands three columns to the left of m.
Each hop divides by 10, so three hops divide by 1,000.
Drop a zero into the hL place, then hop to the kL pin.
Read the kL digit, the point, then all three digits after it.
The left part is whole metres; the right part is what is left in centimetres.
Check it: metres times 100, plus the centimetres, is the whole rope.
Each part is read in the unit of its own last column.
10 dm make 1 m, so the two parts together must give back the whole length.
After the cut, read the three gram digits as one number.
A zero at the front of a number does not change it.
Fill the empty place, then hop three times to the L pin.
Read the litres digit, the point, then all three digits after it.
Fill both empty places, then hop three times to the kg pin.
After the point there must be three digits: fill each empty place.
The g tag moves the digits three places to the right.
Three places to the right makes the measure 1,000 times smaller.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The pins light amber, the point goes back to the unit you have and hops left one place at a time to the want pin, ending on the measure in green.
Phase 2: The pins light amber, the point hops from the smaller unit to the bigger one, a grey zero drops into each empty place, and the decimal turns green.
Phase 3: The Cut handle slides to the gap after the bigger unit's column, the row splits in two, and both parts turn green with their unit tags.
Phase 4: The point hops to the unit asked for, the empty places get their zeros and the unit tag clips on in green; for the two weights each tag is clipped in turn and the digits move three places.

voice.opening: A measure on the chart, and a pin on its unit.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play: pin a unit, hop the point to it, or tap New for another measure.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You hopped left to a bigger unit, and named it.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
